text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000087 bills 99215 far above expectation in every complexity group, but the sampled charts support the billed levels, so the evidence conflicts.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess 99215 share is not explained by panel acuity. It appears in every complexity tier, including patients with no chronic conditions, and the sampled low-complexity 99215s often carry routine diagnoses such as upper respiratory infection, UTI, back pain or follow-up (e.g., C0053883, C0053820, C0053739, C0053743). That pattern is consistent with upcoding. Against this, none of the documented 99215 claims were documented below the billed level, with examples such as C0053846 and C0053979 recorded as high MDM. Taken at face value, that would point to a legitimately complex practice. The ambiguity is whether the notes reflect the visits. The duplicate-note and late-note rates are notable, some notes repeat the same times, and some notes claim moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test line on the claim. This is weak evidence of cloned or inflated documentation, not proof, and with no audit trail and records for under a tenth of claims the chart sample is thin. A reviewer should first request the audit trail and charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed, then compare the duplicate-flagged notes for templated MDM text."}
